title: State relabelling commutes with a run from the initial configuration
statement: Let $tm$ be a multi-tape Turing machine with state set $S$, let $e:S\\simeq S'$ be a bijection, let $x$ be an input word, and let $t\\in\\mathbb{N}$. After $t$ steps from its initial configuration on $x$, the machine obtained by relabelling the states of $tm$ along $e$ has the same configuration as the configuration reached by $tm$ after $t$ steps from its own initial configuration, with the state relabelled by $e$.
hypotheses_covered: A multi-tape Turing machine with state set $S$
replaced:
Let $M$ be a multi-tape Turing machine with $k$ work tapes and state set $S$,
let $e$ be a bijection from $S$ to another state set, let $x$ be an input
word, and let $t \in \mathbb{N}$.  Then the configuration reached by the
machine obtained by relabelling the states of $M$ along $e$ after $t$ steps
from its initial configuration on $x$ equals the configuration that $M$
reaches after $t$ steps from its own initial configuration on $x$, with its
state renamed along $e$.
